title: Scalar-unit normalized tensor comparison for internal modules
statement: Let $R,S$ be commutative condensed rings, $a:R\to S$ a ring-object morphism, and $X$ any scheme. Put $E_X=\operatorname{Ext}_{a_X}$, with its specified adjunction unit $\eta_M:M\to\operatorname{Res}_{a_X}E_XM$ [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-change], [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]. Use the relative tensor of internal modules and its ordinary unbounded derived tensor [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom]. Define the canonical strong monoidal structure of $E_X$ by its unique scalar-unit normalization: for every $M,N$, its comonoidal map $\delta_{M,N}:E_X(M\otimes_{R_X}N)\to E_XM\otimes_{S_X}E_XN$ satisfies $\delta_{M,N}\eta_{M\otimes N}(m\otimes n)=\eta_M(m)\otimes\eta_N(n)$. This is an equality of morphisms after the balanced tensor coprojection, so it refers to generalized tensors, not enough points. The balanced universal property uniquely determines this structure, including its unit; extension preserves flat internal modules. If $E_Z$ is exact for every scheme $Z$, put $T_X=LE_X$ and define $\mu_X:T_X(A\otimes_{R_X}^{\mathrm L}B)\xrightarrow{\sim}T_XA\otimes_{S_X}^{\mathrm L}T_XB$ by the canonical bifunctor-derived lift of $\delta$. Thus on flat-term K-flat representatives its components are the localizations of the signed total of the ordinary map $s\otimes(m\otimes n)\mapsto(s\otimes m)\otimes(1\otimes n)$.

proof.text: Apply the generic normalized strong monoidal extension theorem to the coefficient morphism a_X. For uniqueness, cancel q and use the extension Hom equivalence to show that two normalized structures have equal oplax tensor maps. Their left unit coherence then identifies their unit maps after tensoring with E(R). Tensoring with its invertible unit comparison is cancellable, so the units agree. Injectivity of the oplax data of a strong monoidal structure gives equality of structures.
